newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases under heavy supply.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases under heavy supply.

text.p: NAIROBI, March 12 (Reuter) The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index eased marginally on Wednesday for the third straight session as investors offloaded shares to capitalise on profits, bourse officials said.
The index lost 18.46 points to close at 3415.40. Turnover was posted at 44.183 million shillings on 1,084,356 shares compared to 18.234 million shillings on 367,177 shares on Tuesday.
"Right now, investors are doing a lot of profit-taking especially on their investments in the financials," a senior broker said.
Market prices early this year spiralled upwards as speculators bought ahead of year-end results hoping to make quick gains.
Brokers said they expected continued selling pressure on the financials amid a renewed interest in plantations and industrials.

Meanwhile Kenya Commercial Bank released its long awaited year-end results. It posted a profit of 2.500 billion shillings after tax ($46 million) for the year ended December 31, 1996, compared to 2.372 billion shillings ($43 million) in the previous year.

The bank's pre-tax profit of 4.045 billion shillings was according to projections by market analysts who expected a doubling of the interim pre-tax profit of 2.054 billion shillings released last year.
It will issue a final dividend of 3.50 for a total of 7 Kshs per share, compared to a total of 6 in the previous year.
Barclays Bank was unchanged at 111 while Standard Chartered Bank eased to 46.50 from 47. Kenya Commercial Bank closed at 97 unchanged while National Bank of Kenya shed 15 cents to close at 15.55.
"Kenya Commercial Bank will remain stable because their results have boosted foreign investor confidence by maintaining expected profit levels," a broker said.
A surge in world coffee prices and improved profits has sparked an interest in the plantations which investors hope will be reflected in their earnings for the year.
Sasini Tea & Coffee traded at 75 unchanged while Kakuzi gained a shilling to close at 103.
Brokers said they expected the market to maintain its current selling position for the short term until the books close in May.
"Meanwhile local investors will have to rethink their investment strategies now that most of the results are out and most probably adapt a longer term position," one broker said.
Kenya Breweries was unchanged at 57 while Firestone East Africa closed at 31 unchanged.
